sections.html:
West Fargo lies just west of Fargo in Cass County and is part of the Fargo-Moorhead metro area. The population was 38,626 at the 2020 census and is estimated at 41,175 as of July 1, 2025. Interstate 94, U.S. 10 and U.S. 52 serve the city, and the ZIP code is 58078.

West Fargo Public Schools covers the city, much of southwestern Fargo, Reile's Acres, Horace and Harwood. That matters at tax time, because the combined levy differs depending on which city and school district pair your parcel falls in.

sections.h2: Taxes that must be paid before closing
sections.html:
In Cass County, every current-year property tax has to be paid in full before a deed can be recorded to transfer ownership. Plan for that when you set a closing date, especially in the early months of the year when the new bill comes due. Your title company can tell you the exact figure.

WhenWhat happens in Cass County
First week of DecemberStatements mailed to owners of record as of November 1
January 1Taxes due; current-year taxes must be paid in full to record a deed
By February 155 percent discount on real estate taxes paid in full (not on special assessments or drain taxes)
March 1First installment due
October 15Second installment due, with a 6 percent penalty if unpaid
Prior yearsInterest of 1 percent per month on taxes owed

A deadline that lands on a weekend or county holiday moves to the next business day. If a statement doesn't arrive, contact the county Finance Office at 701-241-5600 or taxes@casscountynd.gov. The schedule is posted on the Cass County property tax page.

sections.h2: How the tax is calculated, and credits
sections.html:
The assessor sets a true and full value. Half of it is the assessed value, and the taxable value of a residential property is 4.5 percent of the true and full value. The county applies the mill levy for your taxing district on top. The county's calculator lists a levy of 306.19 mills for the City of West Fargo, but levies change every year, so rely on your own statement.

  • New construction may qualify for a two-year abatement that takes $150,000 off true and full value when figuring real estate tax. It doesn't reduce special assessments or drain taxes.
  • The Primary Residence Credit can cut the tax obligation by up to $1,600 for an eligible owner with an approved application.

The city assessor reappraises from time to time, and any change shows up on the tax bill you receive the following December. A typical appraisal visit runs 15 to 20 minutes and includes a look inside and outside the house.

West Fargo charges owners for nearby infrastructure through special assessments under Chapter 40 of the North Dakota Century Code. The city's examples include water lines and storage, sewer lines, storm sewer, road and sidewalk paving, and flood protection.

  • The unpaid, uncertified balance is what remains after each year's installment goes to Cass County. Look up a property by address or parcel number on the city's assessor website.
  • Pending specials are estimates for projects still under construction or waiting on final hearings, so the amounts can shift.
  • To pay off a balance, contact the Finance department or send a Special Assessment Payoff Request. Interest builds monthly, so you want an actual payoff figure.
  • The city takes no specials payments between October 1 and November 10, while it certifies installments to the county.
  • Sheyenne Diversion questions go to a separate contact at 701-298-2381.

Ask for payoff numbers early, since a balance generally gets settled at closing. The city finance FAQ has the details.

The city bills water, sewer, garbage and other services monthly, and the account stays in your name until you end service. Fill out the Utility Service Move Out Application with your forwarding address, your closing or moving date and the new owner's name.

Permits come from the Building Department at 2515 Sixth Street E. The building code requires a permit before certain work on existing structures, fees depend on the value of the project, and mechanical permits depend on the type, size and number of appliances. If you finished a basement, replaced a furnace or added a deck, gather those permit records before you list.

The Metro Flood Diversion Authority's project is a large regional effort, described in Cass County's audited financial report as protecting roughly 200,000 people in North Dakota and Minnesota. Voters in Fargo and Cass County approved two dedicated local sales taxes, expected to raise $700 million over their life.

The city lists flood protection among the improvements that special assessments can pay for. If a lender or buyer asks about flood status, check the current map and your assessment statements, and keep records of any flood-related work. Sump pumps, roofing and heating are the usual inspection topics in this climate.

sections.h2: What you must disclose and how you can sell
sections.html:
A seller of a residential dwelling with up to four units provides a written disclosure of material facts before the buyer signs final acceptance, under N.D.C.C. 47-10-02.1. Foreclosure sales, sales by estate fiduciaries and transfers to close relatives are exempt. Section 47-10-02.2 adds a radon disclosure, and section 47-10-02.3 sets ten days from a signed agreement for homeowners association documents.

You can list with an agent, sell on your own or accept a cash offer from a buyer that purchases as-is. Under a tight deadline, such as an inherited property or a pending move, compare net proceeds after taxes, special assessments and any lien payoffs. Cash Home Buyers can review a West Fargo address and explain how an offer works. We don't quote prices here, and you owe nothing if you decline.

In a cash sale, the title company collects the tax and assessment payoffs from your proceeds, you complete the move out application with the closing date, and the deed is recorded once current-year taxes are paid.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay all property taxes before selling in West Fargo?
faqs.a: In Cass County, current-year property taxes must be paid in full before a deed transferring ownership can be recorded. Ask your title company for the exact figure early.

faqs.q: When are Cass County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Statements go out in December and taxes are due January 1. The first installment is due March 1 and the second October 15, with a 6 percent penalty on a late second installment. Paying in full by February 15 earns a 5 percent discount.

faqs.q: Which school district covers West Fargo?
faqs.a: West Fargo Public Schools serves the city, much of southwestern Fargo, Reile's Acres, Horace and Harwood. High schools include West Fargo High School, Sheyenne High, Horace High and Community High.

faqs.q: How do I find my special assessment balance?
faqs.a: Search the city's assessor website by parcel number or address. For a payoff amount, contact Finance or use the Special Assessment Payoff Request form, because interest accrues monthly.

faqs.q: Can I sell a West Fargo house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. You still owe the buyer the written disclosures North Dakota law requires, and the buyer decides whether to accept the property in its current condition.
